title: Sylvan (9d91e3) — failure-mode: invisible control byte in source fooled reviewer AND first-hand verifier; cured by RED-first disproof + escape rewrite
body:
Observation: a code-expert should-fix claimed the G2 containsUnit/containsLesson dedup keys were separator-less string concatenations (silent edge-suppression risk). My first-hand grep/sed verification CONFIRMED the claim — the keys rendered as `${thread.slug}${unit.unitSlug}`. I authored collision tests expecting RED; they passed GREEN against unchanged code.

Diagnosis: the keys carry a literal 0x1F (ASCII unit-separator) byte between the components — invisible in diff, grep, sed, and reviewer rendering. The reviewer and my verification pass were fooled by the same unrenderable byte; only an empirical probe (run the function, expect both edges) plus `od -c` revealed it. Reading source is not always seeing source.

Cure (both halves): (1) behavioural disproof before product-code edits — when a finding predicts a concrete misbehaviour, write the test FIRST and demand RED before "fixing"; a GREEN here refuted the reviewer and my own confirmation. (2) The napkin doctrine generalises beyond PUA sentinels: ANY literal control character in source is a review/verification hazard — write escape sequences. Applied in 8cce69a0: literal byte → visible escape (byte-identical), collision tests pin the behaviour.

Pointer: commit 8cce69a0 (feat/g2-misconception-view); verdict record event 163ca286; probe shape: tsx one-liner + od -c.
